cards.html: This skill fixes the other half: the droplet's git pull. Today it borrows your personal key through agent forwarding. A GitHub deploy key lets the droplet read the LevelUp repo on its own, and nothing more.

A deploy key is an SSH public key that you add to one repository (repo → Settings → Deploy keys), instead of to your account. Differences from your personal key:

Personal key (on your account)Deploy key (on one repo)
ReposEvery repo you can accessOnly this one
AccessRead and writeRead-only unless you tick "Allow write access"
Tied toYouThe repo; it survives if your account keys change
ReuseOne key, many reposGitHub won't accept the same key on a second repo

Leave "Allow write access" unticked. The droplet only ever pulls.

1. On the droplet this time (the key's job is to live there): ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/levelup_repo_ro -C droplet-levelup-ro -N "".
  2. Add levelup_repo_ro.pub as a deploy key on mazharsaif/LevelUp, read-only.
  3. Tell SSH on the droplet to use it for GitHub, in ~/.ssh/config:
Host github.com
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/levelup_repo_ro
  IdentitiesOnly yes

1. Test on the droplet with ssh -T git@github.com: GitHub should greet the deploy key. Then git -C ~/LevelUp pull --ff-only should work in a session without agent forwarding.
  2. Turn off ForwardAgent yes for levelup-droplet in the Mac's ~/.ssh/config, and remove the "No forwarded SSH agent" check from levelup-deploy.

IdentitiesOnly yes matters: without it, SSH may offer other keys first and pick the wrong identity.

BeforeAfter
Deploy works only while your Mac is connected and forwarding its agentThe droplet pulls by itself, from anywhere, at any time
Root on the droplet could use your personal key during a sessionYour personal key never reaches the droplet
A droplet break-in could push to all your reposA droplet break-in can read the LevelUp repo (which it already has a copy of anyway)

This is also what makes automatic deploys possible: GitHub Actions can't forward your Mac's agent, but it doesn't need to any more.

1. Where do you add a deploy key, and what access does it get by default?
  2. Why is the deploy key generated on the droplet, not on the Mac?
  3. What does IdentitiesOnly yes prevent?
  4. Which Mac setting can you turn off once this works?

1. On the repo (Settings → Deploy keys); read-only for that one repo.
  2. The droplet is the only place that needs to use it, so the private key never has to travel.
  3. SSH offering other keys (and maybe the wrong identity) before the one you named.
  4. ForwardAgent yes for levelup-droplet.

o: an SSH key attached to one repository

quiz.q: Give the droplet a read-only deploy key so it can …

o: uses only the key named for that host, not every agent key

quiz.q: Once the droplet has its own deploy key, agent forwarding can be turned off.
quiz.why: Fact: it no longer needs your personal key.
